title: Antineoplastic Activity on Human Glioblastoma Cells and Chemical Profile of Crude Extracts from Giant Deep-Sea Worm Riftia pachyptila
content: Hydrothermal vent communities are a source of bioactive compounds, some of these could be a potential anticancer therapy. Riftia pachyptila is a marine invertebrate endemic to hydrothermal vents. The dichloromethane-methanol (1:1) extracts were obtained from the wall (Pa), the trophosome (Tr), and the tube (Tu) of R. pachyptila. The cytotoxic effect of extracts was evaluated on human glioblastoma cell lines U373, U87, and fibroblast BJ1 cell line, by MTT and trypan blue assays. For detecting DNA apoptotic fragmentation and the tumoral p53 expression by Pa, the tunnel and immunofluorescence assays were performed, respectively. The extracts were analyzed by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. The Pa extract produces the most cytotoxicity on U87 and U373 cells, but not on BJ1 cells; furthermore, Pa extract produced apoptosis and cytosolic p53 stabilization. The chemical profile of extracts showed thirty-four natural compounds. This study identifies R. pachyptila extracts as potential source of drugs for glioblastoma.
